Content: MemorySmith chat is provider-based. IChatProvider isolates model API calls/model discovery/streaming and IChatAgent isolates memory/page context gathering and agent-write behavior. OllamaChatProvider uses /api/chat with stream=true for live chunks and /api/tags for model discovery on the configured Ollama endpoint. GitHubCopilotChatProvider uses GitHub.Copilot.SDK with GitHub CLI auth or token env vars and exposes configured fallback models when SDK discovery is unavailable; the default order prefers free or low-cost GPT candidates first, then Claude Haiku, then Claude Sonnet. GitHub model-unavailable and authentication failures are rewritten in the /chat UI with actionable guidance for refreshing discovered models or configuring GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, COPILOT_API_KEY, GitHubCliPath, or GitHubCliUrl. MemoryChatAgent uses conservative, intent-aware preloading: exact-reply/simple prompts and write-only Agent commands skip local wiki pre-context, explicit MemorySmith/wiki/codebase prompts get a small bounded hybrid/page preload via Chat:MaxPreloadedContextRecords and Chat:MaxPreloadedContextPages, and each item is still capped by Chat:MaxContextItemCharacters. Memory hits are hydrated from full MemoryRecord content instead of only the leading search snippet when they are preloaded. ChatToolCatalog defines shared read-only wiki tool behavior used by both chat interception and MCP endpoints for page search/get and unified search in addition to memory search tools. When preloaded context is absent or insufficient, the prompt lets the model return an app-intercepted MCP-compatible JSON tool request; MemoryChatAgent recognizes toolCalls or JSON-RPC tools/call payloads, runs read-only local wiki tools, adds Local MemorySmith tool results to the same provider turn, tracks those accessed resources as ChatContextOrigins.Tool, and asks for the final answer without exposing tool JSON to the user. Supported chat-side tools are memorysmith_unified_search, memorysmith_search, memorysmith_semantic_search, memorysmith_hybrid_search, memorysmith_context_pack, memorysmith_get, memorysmith_page_search, and memorysmith_page_get. ChatIntentInterceptor can also pre-run clear wiki intents (such as unified search, context pack retrieval, or page fetch) before provider generation, and those intercepted resources are also shown as tool-accessed resources. Stream updates include structured trace events with tool metadata, duration, and token estimates. The chat UI renders a global Trace panel with a compact execution graph, filters, collapsible trace headers, interleaved reasoning segments, preloaded context summaries, tool call requests, tool results, and assistant output so users can inspect turn internals without reading raw JSON blobs. The Trace panel keeps history visible on medium-width editor layouts by moving below the history/chat row, only hides history on narrower trace-open layouts, and synchronizes selected history chats to the most recent inspectable turn. Tool-call trace entries keep editable JSON arguments and can be rerun from the panel; rerun results append to the same turn and add touched resources as tool context. ChatRunControl supports an icon Finish Step soft stop that lets the current provider/tool step finish before stopping the loop, while the icon Stop control remains immediate cancellation. Chat:ToolCallsEnabled, Chat:MaxToolIterations, Chat:MaxToolCallsPerTurn, and Chat:MaxToolResultCharacters bound the loop. Agent mode can parse structured provider output and propose MemoryRecord entries and Data/Pages markdown pages when Chat:AgentWritesEnabled is true; the /chat UI requests approval mode, stores proposed writes on the turn, and requires explicit approve/reject actions in the Trace side panel before applying writes through IChatAgent.ApplyAgentWritesAsync. Tool calls remain read-only. Image attachments are saved to trusted temp files and passed as native image payloads to providers that support images. Usage metadata flows through ChatUsageSummary: Ollama final chunks can report prompt/eval token counts, GitHub SDK usage/context events can report context-window and quota snapshots, and MemoryChatAgent estimates token usage when providers do not report it. The /chat UI supports provider/model selection, persisted provider/model/mode and active chat, streamed response text with elapsed timers and per-response durations, assistant turn model metadata such as Ollama / Athena or GitHub / gpt-4.1, a bottom-right context usage meter with optional provider rate/quota text, icon Stop and Finish Step controls with tooltips, Send on Enter, file and clipboard image attachments with explicit X remove buttons, retained per-chat drafts/queued attachments, delete-chat confirmation, compact chat history titles, thinking content anchored above the visible answer with active animation, local chat history, and clickable memory/page resource chips. Default preloaded context chips retain the neutral wiki-chip styling, mid-chat/intercepted tool resources use a blue chip theme, and created pages remain green write chips. The design leaves room for OpenAI, Anthropic, or other providers without changing the UI or agent workflow.
Title: Chat Agent Provider Architecture
